title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over attempt to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
summary:
Moscow suspected of being behind plan to kill Kyivstoner before a performance in Denmark

Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attaché in Copenhagen would be expelled after…
byline: Guardian staff and agencies in Copenhagen

blocks.text: Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attaché in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper.

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attaché from Denmark” within seven days, Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference.
“We are saying this very clearly: we have exposed you,” he said.

The announcement came after Danish police said they had averted an attempt by Russian intelligence services ⁠to kill the US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner in September before a planned performance in Denmark.
Rasmussen also said that Denmark was mulling suspending Schengen visas to Russians.
“We have launched work at the European level to further tighten the rules governing access of Russian nationals to Europe,” he said.
“We are now stepping up our efforts towards a halt to all non-essential visas.”
“The strongest response Denmark can give is not to waver and to support Ukraine. And we fully intend to continue supporting Ukraine,” he said.

Police ⁠thwarted the alleged ⁠plot when ​they arrested three men with links to the Danish criminal underworld shortly before the rapper was due to give a ⁠concert on 25 September, which was then cancelled, officials said. Kyvistoner, whose real name is Albert Viktorovich Vasiliev, holds both US and Ukrainian nationality.

“It is our clear assessment that the assassination attempt was planned by the Russian ⁠intelligence services,” Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen, head of Denmark’s national security and intelligence service, PET, told a ​press conference.

According to prosecutors, the suspects were driving towards the concert venue north of Copenhagen with two loaded pistols and two knives when police arrested them at about 9.55pm (1955 GMT), five minutes before the concert was due ‌to begin. A fourth suspect was arrested later that evening, police said.
One of the suspects had bought a ticket to the concert, according ​to the charges.

The suspects are charged under Section 108 of Denmark’s Criminal Code, which covers assisting a foreign intelligence service, as well as attempted murder. They denied wrongdoing in court, broadcaster DR reported.
“A Russian assassination attempt is not something we’ve seen in Denmark before, ⁠and that gives me an impression of an increasingly aggressive and ​risk-taking Russia,” Kieffer-Kristensen said.
“We believe ​that the case is important ​for understanding the threat that Denmark faces from Russia.”
